# Workbooks

> Workbooks is a software ecosystem and systems architecture where people and
> AI build together — and what they build runs anywhere, stays connected, and
> keeps getting better. The core unit is a workbook: a single HTML file that
> carries a whole piece of software (interface, code, data, history) and opens
> anywhere a browser does. The Nexus is the engine you own that runs workbooks
> (laptop or cloud) and makes them isolated, stateful, and agentic. Toolkits
> are real programs compiled to WebAssembly wrapped in readable manuals that
> teach people and agents alike.

The CLI is `wbx` (installed via https://workbooks.sh/install.sh). With a
coding agent, install the skills: `npx skills add workbooks-sh/workbooks.sh`.

## Learn
- [What is a workbook](https://workbooks.sh/learn/workbook.html): the unit — one file that is a whole piece of software
- [What is the Nexus](https://workbooks.sh/learn/nexus.html): the engine — docking makes a file isolated, stateful, agentic
- [What is a toolkit](https://workbooks.sh/learn/toolkit.html): the parts — wasm programs whose manual is the interface
- [Org](https://workbooks.sh/learn/org.html): the written layer people and agents share
- [Agents](https://workbooks.sh/learn/agents.html): long-running crew — a model on a schedule with files, tools, memory
- [The Autopoet](https://workbooks.sh/learn/autopoet.html): the gardener — tends the declarative layer, never the engine

## Try
- [hello-workbook.html](https://workbooks.sh/learn/hello-workbook.html): a real workbook that explains itself — live WebAssembly inside
- [Source](https://github.com/workbooks-sh/workbooks.sh): Apache-2.0, open forever
